name: Question 7
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/7c959b9c517b17d9427de450def510b9673d91fd951e28696d4d56d8a768b74d.png)

Change the order of integration in the integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $y,$ then $x,$ and then $z.$ The integration region $R$ is shown above.
worked_solution:
We wish to find limits of integration ${u}_{1}(x,z),$ ${u}_{2}(x,z),$ ${v}_{1}(z),$ ${v}_{2}(z),$ $a,$ and $b$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{2},\,\,0\le x\le {y}^{2}}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z,$ we write $R$ as a type III region and its projection $D$ onto the $xz$-plane as a type II *plane* region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $y$-axis and in the direction of increasing $y,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/c3837a3551b35a5146fd2c8e2441e4a9d6d947e8c52e44254d48eb854e54e605.png)

The arrow enters the region through the left boundary and leaves through the right boundary:

- The left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x,z),$ is

$$
x={y}^{2}\,⟹\,y=\sqrt{x}.
$$

- The right boundary of the region is

$$
y=\sqrt{2}.
$$

Therefore, the type III representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,\sqrt{x}\le y\le \sqrt{2}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/22581a56f4d9cb611bd9a58b06b1036cd47b500217570ae6890d0f38dba6742c.png)

We now consider the projection $D$ as a type II plane region in the $xz$-plane with the right curve given by 

$$
{\begin{aligned}y=\sqrt{x} \\ y=\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\sqrt{x}=\sqrt{2}\,⟹\,x=2.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/e2305d3da63886703666fd58a2adfe8f15f2eceb7261922f46ba4949b0fc0cde.png)

Hence, we have that

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 1}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to $y,$ then $x,$ then $z,$ we obtain

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{\sqrt{x}}^{\sqrt{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z.
$$

Question 7

Change the order of integration in the integral ∫01∫02∫0y2f(x,y,z)dxdydz. so that it is integrated first with respect to y, then x, and then z. The integration region R is shown above.

a
 ∫01∫02∫x2f(x,y,z)dydxdz
b
 ∫01∫0x∫x2f(x,y,z)dydxdz
c
 ∫01∫02∫x2xf(x,y,z)dydxdz
d
 ∫01∫0x∫x2f(x,y,z)dydxdz
e
 ∫01∫01∫x2f(x,y,z)dydxdz
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We wish to find limits of integration u1(x,z), u2(x,z), v1(z), v2(z), a, and b such that

∫01∫02∫0y2f(x,y,z)dxdydz=∫ab∫v1(z)v2(z)∫u1(x,z)u2(x,z)f(x,y,z)dydxdz.

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration R can be written as a type II region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):0≤z≤1,0≤y≤2,0≤x≤y2}

To change the order of integration from dxdydz to dydxdz, we write R as a type III region and its projection D onto the xz-plane as a type II plane region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the y-axis and in the direction of increasing y, as shown below.

The arrow enters the region through the left boundary and leaves through the right boundary:

  • The left boundary of the region, written in the form y=y(x,z), is x=y2⟹y=x.

  • The right boundary of the region is y=2.

Therefore, the type III representation of R is

R={(x,y,z):(x,z)∈D,x≤y≤2},

as shown in the diagram below.

We now consider the projection D as a type II plane region in the xz-plane with the right curve given by

{y=xy=2⟹x=2⟹x=2.

Hence, we have that D={(x,z):0≤x≤2,0≤z≤1}.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to y, then x, then z, we obtain ∫01∫02∫0y2f(x,y,z)dxdydz=∫01∫02∫x2f(x,y,z)dydxdz.
